Read-only review (Opus). Not built here.

**Verdict: Needs changes before merge.**

The merge commit 5103ecce1 is clean: `git show --remerge-diff 5103ecce1` is empty. The change is in a29d79a65. The PR keeps `held-for-merge`. No agent merges it.

### Blockers

1. `crates/geometry/src/step_csys_read.rs:28-30` with `crates/geometry/src/step_units.rs:37-62`: a legal short-name file can now give a different tool position without a refusal.
   - solidcore's Part 21 parser maps ISO 10303-21 short names to long names (`SHORT_NAMES` in `solidcore-record/src/step/p21.rs:614-659` at the pinned rev 2016386). The table maps `A2PL3D`, `CRTPNT`, `DRCTN`, `LNGUNT`, `CNBSUN` and `LMWU`. It does not map `GLOBAL_UNIT_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT` or `SI_UNIT`.
   - ruststep kept the short names as written. Thus the old reader found no `AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D` in a short-name file, and the tool body fell back to numeric placement with the reason "the file names no coordinate systems".
   - The new reader finds the CIP in such a file. But `mm_per_unit` finds no `GLOBAL_UNIT_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT`, returns `Ok(None)`, and `read` uses `unwrap_or(1.0)`. A short-name tool file in inches or metres now gives a CIP origin and a tip offset at the wrong scale (25.4 or 1000 times), with no refusal.
   - What must change: refuse when no context states a length unit but the file has a `LENGTH_UNIT` record (the parser maps `LNGUNT` to it). Alternatively, refuse a coordinate-system read when the unit context cannot be found. Add a pin: a short-name tool file with an inch unit is refused by name (or reads at 25.4 mm per unit), never at 1 mm per unit.

### Notes

- Semantics, compared line by line with the deleted `step_csys.rs`, `step_units.rs` and `step_diag.rs`: these are the same. The entities that the reader follows, the `$`/`*` defaults (+Z axis, +X ref direction), the normalisation, the orthogonalisation (x = r - (r.z)z, parallel refused at 1e-9), y = z x x, the SI prefix table, the conversion chain and its cap (`MAX_CHAIN` 4, a cycle is refused), the refusal of an unknown prefix, of a non-metre SI unit and of two different units, complex instances (`Entity::record` finds the part by name), typed values and `.MILLI.` enumerations (trimmed and in upper case on both sides).
- `real()` now looks through at most 4 typed wrappers (before: no limit). A deeper value gives a refusal, not a different number.
- Lower-case keywords: ruststep refused them as a syntax error. The new parser reads them in upper case and gives the correct values. This is a new reading, not a wrong number.
- `\X2\` names are now decoded. An ISO 13399 name has no escapes, so the classification does not change for real files.
- Several DATA sections: the old reader used only the first section, also for the unit. A file with its unit context in a second section was read at 1 mm per unit. The new reading is correct. A disagreement between sections is refused ("two length units").
- Duplicate ids: the split is sound. The tool-body read refuses by name (`step_csys_read.rs:122-138`), because the two readings can place the tool at two places. The silent "first wins" of the model import comes from #2904 and the kernel, not from this PR.
- A file with no DATA section keeps the old text. The new syntax-error text is the model-import wording. No test asserted the old text.
- Robustness: the new files have no `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic` outside tests. The slice indexes in `step_diag.rs` (lines 43, 95, 140, 176, 178) are moved code, and their bounds are at ASCII positions or are checked. Reference following is one level deep, and unit chains are capped. The parser caps the size, the entities, the records, the parameters and the depth. ruststep had no caps.
- `step_depth::check` runs in front of every parser call on both app paths: `step.rs` before `step_diag::locate`, and the `step_csys` wrapper before the read. The unit reader is not called from the model import (solidcore reads the units there). The public geometry functions have no scan, but the parser's own depth cap of 64 bounds the stack.
- `step_diag::locate`: one probe parse for each record, and each probe is linear in its record. The total cost is linear, not quadratic. There is no cancel check, as before this PR.
- Layering: `pub use ::solidcore_step::p21` is in the kernel. The app and the UI do not depend on `camcraft-kernel`, so they cannot name solidcore types. The geometry API gives only plain types. `ruststep` is gone from `crates/app/Cargo.toml` and from the app sources (comments only). The `Cargo.lock` diff is only that edge. There is no new `camcraft-*` edge.
- wasm32: `read_tool_csys` and the model import both refuse STEP by name. Thus the locator, which lets every record through there, cannot hide a refusal that the desktop build gives. The browser build loses the tool coordinate-system read, which ruststep gave before. This is a refusal, not a wrong value.
- Tests: the four moved unit tests keep the same asserts. The `#[test]` count goes up by 13 (17 added, 4 removed), as the body says. The pins prove what their names say. The comment at `crates/geometry/tests/step_csys_read.rs:110` says "a unit that loops", but that case is in `step_units.rs`. The Gate map lines name `camcraft_geometry::*`. All files are under 400 lines. Each new module has a provenance line.
- `crates/kernel/src/solidcore_step.rs:244` still points to "crates/app's `step_units`". It is now in `camcraft-geometry`.
- Outside this PR: the model import's unit read (`length_units` in the kernel, and solidcore's units module) also looks for `GLOBAL_UNIT_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT` by its long name only. A short-name model in inches can thus import at the wrong scale. I recommend a separate issue.
- PR body: complete, with a `Changelog:` line, and ends with `Fixes #2789`. There is no closing keyword for #917 or #2790.

Addressed (head 4b694c7c7e40aac4003c1eb49113e6d7e04c17b9).

Commit 9221ccc65 has the fix. Merge 4b694c7c7 brings in `origin/main` (with #2024). The merge had no conflict.

**Blocker (unit context of a short-name tool file):** fixed by a refusal.
- `mm_per_unit` (`crates/geometry/src/step_units.rs`) refuses by name when no `GLOBAL_UNIT_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT` states a length unit but the file has one of these records:
  - a `LENGTH_UNIT` (the parser maps `LNGUNT` to it);
  - an `SI_UNIT` of the metre;
  - a `CONVERSION_BASED_UNIT` over a `LENGTH_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT`.
- The text is "length unit #N is in the file, but no GLOBAL_UNIT_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT states a length unit (the unit context is missing, or it is written in a form this reader does not read)". The tool-body read adds the prefix "length unit: ".
- A file with no unit record keeps 1 mm per unit, as the ruststep reader did. Angle units alone are no length unit.
- The reader does not read the short forms of `GLOBAL_UNIT_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT` and `SI_UNIT`. No public source in the repository or in the solidcore checkout states them, and a guessed name gives a guessed scale.
- Pins (`crates/geometry/tests/step_csys_read.rs`):
  - `a_short_name_tool_file_in_inches_or_metres_is_refused_by_name`;
  - `a_short_name_tool_file_with_a_long_unit_context_reads_at_its_scale`;
  - `a_long_name_tool_file_in_inches_reads_at_twenty_five_point_four`;
  - `a_tool_file_with_no_unit_record_keeps_millimetres`.
- Pin (`crates/geometry/tests/step_units.rs`): `a_length_unit_that_no_context_states_is_refused_by_name`.
- The decision is in `docs/decisions/2789-step-readers-solidcore.md`.

**Notes:**
- `#[test]` count: the body now says +18 (22 added, 4 removed).
- `crates/geometry/tests/step_csys_read.rs`: the comment now names only the self-referencing placement, and it points to the `step_units` suite for the unit that loops.
- `crates/kernel/src/solidcore_step.rs:244`: the comment now names `camcraft_geometry::step_units`.
- The model import's unit read stays in #2919, a separate PR. I commented the parser and kernel facts on #2919.

**Gate on 4b694c7c7:**
- geometry `step_units`, `step_csys_read` and `step_diag`: 21 passed.
- app `tool_csys`, `step_nesting`, `tool_body` and `mcp_tool_body`: 37 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-kernel -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- The batch tier was not run here.

Read-only delta review (Opus). Not built here.

**Verdict for the whole PR at this head: Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

This verdict replaces the verdict of the review of 5103ecce1. The batch gate of this head is reported separately. The PR keeps `held-for-merge`. No agent merges it.

Scope: commit 9221ccc65 and the merge 4b694c7c7. `git show --remerge-diff 4b694c7c7` is empty. Thus the merge of main has no hand edits.

### The blocker of the first review: met

`mm_per_unit` (`crates/geometry/src/step_units.rs:38-48`) now refuses by name when no `GLOBAL_UNIT_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT` states a length unit, but the file has a length-unit record (`unstated_length_unit`, lines 58-76). The evidence is one of these records: a `LENGTH_UNIT`, an `SI_UNIT` of the metre, or a `CONVERSION_BASED_UNIT` whose measure is a `LENGTH_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT`. The parser at the pinned rev 2016386 maps `LNGUNT`, `CNBSUN` and `LMWU` to these long names (`SHORT_NAMES`, `solidcore-record/src/step/p21.rs:614-651`). `Exchange::entities` is a `BTreeMap`, so the first id in the text is deterministic.

The result for each case, from the code:

- (a) Long names, inch context: 25.4 mm for each unit. Pinned by `a_long_name_tool_file_in_inches_reads_at_twenty_five_point_four`.
- (b) Long names, metre context: 1000 mm for each unit. Pinned by the moved `step_units` tests and by `a_short_name_tool_file_with_a_long_unit_context_reads_at_its_scale` (inch, metre, millimetre).
- (c) Short-name geometry with `LNGUNT`, and a unit context that the parser does not map: refused, "length unit #12 is in the file, but no GLOBAL_UNIT_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT states a length unit ...". Pinned by `a_short_name_tool_file_in_inches_or_metres_is_refused_by_name`.
- (d) A short-name file in which the length unit has no mapped name at all: the reader sees no length-unit record and reads 1 mm for each unit. See note 1. This case needs a file whose length unit is not a `LENGTH_UNIT` instance. ISO 10303-41 makes each SI or conversion-based length unit a `LENGTH_UNIT`, and its ISO short name `LNGUNT` is mapped. Thus a conforming file cannot get to this case. It is the same reading as case (e), so it is not a blocker.
- (e) No unit record at all: 1 mm for each unit. This is the same as the ruststep reader (`git show a29d79a65^:crates/app/src/geometry/import/step_csys.rs:240-242`, `Ok(None)` read as 1.0). Pinned by `a_tool_file_with_no_unit_record_keeps_millimetres`. That test also asserts that no `_UNIT` text stays in the file.
- (f) A context that states only angle units: if the file has a length unit beside it, the read is refused. If the file has only angle units (a radian, a degree), the result is `Ok(None)`. Both are pinned by `a_length_unit_that_no_context_states_is_refused_by_name`.
- (g) Two contexts that disagree: refused, "the file states two length units". The code and the pin (`contexts_that_disagree_or_a_unit_that_cannot_be_read_refuse_by_name`) did not change.

### Other checks

- The refusal is an `Err(String)`. No panic. `step_csys_read.rs:28-30` adds the prefix "length unit: ". The app wrapper maps it to `ImportError::Step` (`crates/app/src/geometry/import/step_csys.rs:26`). `from_step_auto`, `tool_body_assembly` and `tool_body_view` show it as "coordinate systems unreadable: ...".
- Tests: the delta only adds tests and changes one comment. No existing assert changed. The count in the body is correct: 22 added (11 + 6 + 4 + 1), 4 removed, net +18.
- No new `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic` outside tests. The four `expect` calls in the delta are in tests. File sizes at this head: `step_units.rs` 178, `step_csys_read.rs` 208, `tests/step_csys_read.rs` 207, `tests/step_units.rs` 127, `solidcore_step.rs` 349 lines.
- The notes of the first review are met. The `step_csys_read.rs` test comment now names only the self-referencing placement. The kernel comment at `solidcore_step.rs:244` now names `camcraft_geometry::step_units`.
- The body names #2919 as the follow-up, with no closing keyword. It still ends with `Fixes #2789`. #917 has only `Refs`. #2790 and #2919 have no closing keyword.
- The decision file has the new entry, the dropped options and the pins.

### Notes

1. Case (d) residual: a nonconforming short-name file with a simple `SI_UNIT` short form of the metre and no `LNGUNT` is read at 1 mm for each unit. The old reader found no CIP in such a file. I recommend a hardening on #2919 or a new `P7` issue: refuse a coordinate-system read when no context states a length unit and the file has an entity name that the parser did not map. This is not a blocker, because a conforming file cannot get to this case.
2. New refusal on long-name files: a file whose context lists only angle units, but that has a millimetre `LENGTH_UNIT` record, was read at 1 mm before. It is now refused. This is safe (a refusal, not a wrong value), and the decision file covers it.
3. In `tool_body_view`, the mesh of a short-name inch file still goes through the model import. That scale gap is in #2919, not in this PR.
4. Pins (c) and (e) use hand-made text, not real vendor tool files. The body says so under "Not exercised".
